metadata.subject: Computer Networks
metadata.title: Read IP Addresses
metadata.description: Validate IPv4 addresses and use them to identify packet endpoints.

learning_objectives: Recognize the four-octet structure of an IPv4 address.
Use a destination address to identify the receiving device.

mission.title: Reason with IPv4 addresses
mission.description: Make a prediction, then let the address model check the consequence.

introduction.title: An address for each endpoint
introduction.content: An IPv4 address is four numbers separated by dots. Each number must be from 0 to 255. A packet uses the destination address to identify where it should go.

worked_example.title: Match the destination
worked_example.content: Read the packet's complete destination address, then compare it with every displayed endpoint.
worked_example.conclusion: The complete address—not just one number—identifies the matching endpoint.

action_explanations.validate-address: You checked all four octets instead of trusting the address shape alone.
action_explanations.construct-address: You kept the generated octets in order and separated them with dots.
action_explanations.identify-endpoints: The packet contains both a source and destination address.
action_explanations.route-packet: The destination address matched exactly one device.

task.prompt: Construct the IPv4 address from these four octets.
Identify the packet's source and destination addresses.
Use the destination address to choose the receiving device.

challenge.title: Address matching challenge
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep experimenting with the address model.

phases.title: Choose the endpoint
phases.instruction: Match the full destination address to one device.
phases.feedback: Compare all four destination octets with every device.

items.content: IPv4 needs exactly four octets, each from 0 to 255.

phases.title: Validate IPv4
phases.instruction: Decide whether the generated address is valid.
phases.feedback: Check octet count, characters, and range.

phases.title: Construct IPv4
phases.instruction: Turn the octets into one correct address.

phases.title: Identify endpoints
phases.feedback: Do not swap source and destination.

phases.title: Route by address
phases.instruction: Choose the one device whose address matches the packet.

thinking.title: Predict a hidden endpoint
thinking.instruction: Inspect the device addresses and packet. The destination endpoint remains hidden.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not guess from device order; compare the complete address.

feedback.all_correct: You matched the hidden destination correctly.
feedback.incorrect: Compare every octet with the device addresses.

discovery.title: Address discovery
discovery.summary: IPv4 uses four bounded octets, and the complete destination address identifies a packet's receiving endpoint.

sections.title: WHAT?
sections.content: An IPv4 address identifies a network interface using four dotted numbers.

sections.title: VALID RANGE
sections.content: Every octet must be a whole number from 0 to 255.

sections.title: WHY?
sections.content: Packets carry source and destination addresses so networks know where traffic starts and ends.

sections.title: REMEMBER
sections.content: Match the entire address, not one familiar-looking octet.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of street addresses
alternate_explanations.content: A complete street address identifies one destination; one number alone is not enough.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through a packet
alternate_explanations.content: Destination 10.0.0.42 matches the camera with 10.0.0.42, so that camera receives the packet.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how does an IPv4 destination address help deliver a packet?
recall.model_answer: The destination IPv4 address identifies the endpoint that should receive the packet.
